text:
Early morning at the Thessaly Weir, and the Morrow arrives the way it always has, brown and unhurried, only to meet a concrete lip that sends a good share of it sideways into a new channel. Fog hangs over the gates. Nothing about the scene announces that a landscape has been rearranged.

The Thessaly Weir diverts the Morrow, and has done so in earnest since 14 March 2019, when the diversion was formally confirmed. It redirects roughly 38 percent of the river's average annual flow, about 12 cubic meters per second, away from its old course.

Dr. Imelda Vantross, chief hydrological engineer at the Lower Carrow Water Authority, certified the arrangement. Her judgment rests on the Authority's Thessaly Weir Commissioning Review, Document LCWA-19/07, presented at the public inquiry in Dunmarsh.

Rivers, one reflects, are rarely finished things. The Morrow has simply been given a second road.
